sources.title: Introducing GPT-5 for developers
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. August 7, 2025 launch identifies gpt-5 as the API reasoning model, separate from ChatGPT routing and gpt-5-chat-latest. Its three API size tiers, reasoning-effort controls, benchmark results and pricing supply no numerical total or active parameter specification.

sources.title: GPT-5 model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact full Markdown freshly fetched October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200) and independently retrieved through official documentation. Alias defaults to gpt-5-2025-08-07; documents 400,000 context, 272,000 maximum input, 128,000 maximum output, text/image inputs, text output, reasoning tokens, function calling, file uploads and prompt caching. No total or active parameter count is supplied. Alias and snapshot are Deprecated, not shut down.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Complete Markdown fetched. PDF ingestion is supported on vision-capable models and sends extracted text plus page images to the model. Combined with exact GPT-5 image-input, file-upload and Responses support, this establishes PDF as an API document format rather than a native sensory modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: June 11, 2026 notice explicitly lists gpt-5 and gpt-5-2025-08-07 for shutdown December 11, 2026. This is scheduled retirement, not evidence of completed shutdown or an endpoint runtime check.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current terms effective January 1, 2026 apply to API services; sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited use and reserve service intellectual property. Supports descriptive Proprietary classification of hosted access, not a downloadable-weight license or a claim these exact terms governed the August 2025 launch.

sources.title: All models
sources.evidence: Current indexed official catalog separates the hosted GPT-5 entry from the open-weight category, which explicitly lists gpt-oss models under Apache 2.0. Read with the API launch and service terms; no GPT-5 checkpoint download is supplied.

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Original full PDF freshly fetched October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200); complete extracted text searched for parameter/size disclosures and introduction/training sections inspected. Section 1 maps the API to gpt-5-thinking and distinguishes ChatGPT model routing; Table 1 names model progressions, not unchanged-base lineage or numerical sizes. Section 2 describes RL training. No total or active parameter count is supplied; system routing does not disclose internal expert routing.

sources.title: From Hard Refusals to Safe-Completions: Toward Output-Centric Safety Training
sources.evidence: Original full PDF freshly fetched October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200); complete extracted text searched and Section 3.1 inspected. Production GPT-5 Thinking (gpt5-r) differs from o3 along architecture and training axes. The o4-mini-like controlled experiments hold their own architectures constant, but do not establish GPT-5 lineage or size. No numerical total or active production count is supplied.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking System Card Addendum
sources.evidence: Later November 12, 2025 addendum freshly fetched October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200); full text and comparison tables rechecked. It explicitly compares gpt-5-thinking with GPT-5.1, but reports safety scores without total or active parameter counts. A successor comparison does not establish a count-preserving base relationship.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Complete Markdown fetched. Archived guide applies to models before GPT-5.6 and explains OpenAI prompt caching through Transformer attention layers and stored key/value tensors. The exact GPT-5 model page explicitly supports prompt caching. Their conjunction supports broad Transformer attention as an operational inference, without asserting a complete layer inventory or dense/MoE routing; table examples for nano and GPT-5.2 are not transferred.

sources.title: Studying metagaming latents in language models
sources.evidence: Later interpretability research was checked because it mentions GPT-5. Its internal residual-stream/SAE experiments study an o3 reinforcement-learning run; GPT-5 is only the grader. These findings do not disclose GPT-5 architecture or parameter counts.

sources.title: Learning Powerful Models: From Transformers to Reasoners and Beyond
sources.evidence: October 8, 2025 official researcher talk describes current GPT decoder attention and reasoning-token computation within Transformer context, naming GPT-5 among reasoners. This is broad corroborating context, not a snapshot-specific architecture report or a parameter disclosure; the operational architecture inference rests on s2 and s10.

sources.title: Reasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought
sources.publisher: Chen Yueh-Han et al.; OpenAI, NYU, UCL, UPenn and MATS
sources.evidence: Later original research reopened October 27, 2026; original full PDF and complete cached text searched. Figure 1(a) evaluates GPT-5, but Figure 1(b) and the parameter-scaling analysis concern Qwen3 and gpt-oss open-weight models. Neither total nor active GPT-5 parameters are reported; their counts cannot transfer to GPT-5.

sources.title: ZAYA1-8B Technical Report
sources.evidence: May 6, 2026 original model-team report reopened October 27, 2026. Table XI explicitly separates Active and Total parameters and leaves both cells as dashes for GPT-5-High. Caption says its GPT-5 comparison row is reproduced from the DeepSeek-V3.2 report; no numerical GPT-5 count or independently measured count is supplied.

sources.title: Cleaning Maintenance Logs with LLM Agents for Improved Predictive Maintenance
sources.publisher: University of Luxembourg; Valeriu Dimidov et al.; PHM Society 2025
sources.evidence: Original empirical research reopened October 27, 2026. Section 4.5 explicitly says OpenAI does not disclose GPT-5 parameter counts or internal sparsity. Its black-box dense treatment is the authors' benchmarking assumption, not architecture evidence; Table 4 reports context/pricing, not a total or active count.

name.note: Official API model name; this record is not the ChatGPT multi-model system or gpt-5-chat-latest.

developer.note: OpenAI publishes and releases the exact API model.

family.note: The developer launch groups gpt-5, mini and nano within GPT-5; normalize the specific family instead of generic gpt.

release_date.note: Dated first-party launch explicitly makes the API model available that day; the matching immutable snapshot corroborates identity.

open_weights.note: Hosted proprietary API release with no public checkpoint distribution; official model catalog distinguishes the separate open-weight offerings.

license.note: Descriptive classification of closed service/model access, not an SPDX checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 primary-source and bounded later-research searches found no supported nominal total for the exact gpt-5 reasoning API model. Original cards and training research give no numeric count or count-preserving named base; Zyphra Table XI leaves GPT-5-High Total blank. Size tiers, successor comparisons and speculative estimates cannot establish a total.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked separately for active/activated parameters in original and later research. Zyphra Table XI explicitly leaves GPT-5-High Active blank; the OpenAI CoT study reports parameter scaling only for separate open-weight models. No supported active count or internal expert-routing specification was found. Reasoning effort, service routing and a benchmark author's dense assumption do not establish active parameters.

architecture.note: Broad classification is an explicit cross-source operational inference: exact GPT-5 supports prompt caching, and the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 guide describes that mechanism as Transformer attention with key/value tensors. This does not establish an exhaustive block inventory, exclusively Transformer layers, dense/MoE feed-forward routing or counts. The researcher talk is corroborating context only.

context_window.note: Exact total context is 400,000 tokens. Maximum input 272,000 and maximum output 128,000 are separately documented limits, not alternative context values or binary expansions.

modalities.note: Native inputs are text/image and output text. PDF is added under the catalog supported-API-file convention: extracted text and page images are passed to the model. Hosted image-generation tools do not imply native image output.

reasoning.note: Exact API release is the thinking model with internal reasoning-token support and minimal/low/medium/high effort settings. Minimal remains a reasoning setting and is distinct from the non-reasoning chat model.

tool_call.note: Launch and model documentation explicitly support function calling and custom tools; not inferred merely from generic agentic benchmarks.

description.value: Reasoning model with text and image input, text output, a 400,000-token context window and function calling.
description.note: Replace workhorse framing with directly documented behavior and capacity, without unsupported size or current-best claims.

patch.notes: The gpt-5 alias defaults to gpt-5-2025-08-07, the reasoning API model released August 7, 2025; it is distinct from ChatGPT routing and gpt-5-chat-latest. Context is 400,000 tokens, with separate 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output limits. PDF files are processed into text and page images. Broad Transformer attention is inferred from exact-model prompt-caching support and its documented mechanism. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; later Zyphra comparisons leave both GPT-5 counts blank. Complete structure and dense/MoE routing are undisclosed. OpenAI schedules this alias and snapshot for API shutdown December 11, 2026; no live endpoint request was made.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retained explicit null total and active counts after reopening the exact API specifications, launch, original system/training papers and later GPT-5.1, CoT-control and Zyphra comparisons. Zyphra Table XI supplies explicit Active/Total columns but no GPT-5 values; neither a supported nominal count nor count-preserving lineage was found. Preserved the other 12 field assessments.
